compared: PRH samples with different Archimedean copulas

quote: Corollary 3.9. Suppose X1, . . . , Xn and X∗1, . . . , X∗n are independent samples with Xi ~ ENH(α1, λ1, βi), and Xi∗ ~ ENH(α2, λ2, βi∗), i = 1, . . . , n. Then for α1 ≤ α2 and λ > 0, we have Σi=1^n βi = Σi=1^n βi∗ ⟹ Xn:n ≥Lorenz X∗n:n.

quote: Theorem 3.10. For X ~ ES(α, λ, φ1) and X∗ ~ ES(α∗, λ, φ2), if ψ2 ◦ φ1 is super-additive, then α ≽w α∗ implies X1:n ≤st X∗1:n.
family: Exponentiated-scale ES(α, λ): H(x) = [G(λx)]^α, arbitrary absolutely continuous baseline G; components dependent through Archimedean copulas with generators φ1, φ2 (ψi = φi^{-1} pseudo-inverse)
compared: two dependent samples with possibly different copulas
ambiguity: Extends Bashkar et al. [3] Theorem 4.1 (common copula case) to different dependence structures; notation X ~ ES(α, λ, φ) denotes the sample with ES marginals and copula generator φ.

quote: Theorem 3.2. Let X1, . . . , Xn (X∗1, . . . , X∗n) be independent random variables with Xi ~ ENH(αi, λ, β) (X∗i ~ ENH(αi∗, λ, β)), i = 1, . . . , n. Then, for any λ, β > 0, we have (α1, . . . , αn) ≽w (α∗1, . . . , α∗n) ⟹ Xn:n ≥st X∗n:n.
family: Exponentiated Nadarajah–Haghighi ENH(α, λ, β): F(x) = [1 − e^{1−(1+λx)^α}]^β, x ≥ 0; heterogeneous outer shape αi, common λ, β
compared: shape vectors α vs α* under weak supermajorization
ambiguity: The printed relation is '≽w' (weak supermajorization, superscript w): consistent with G_{Xn:n} increasing and Schur-concave in α.

quote: Theorem 3.3. Let X1, . . . , Xn (X∗1, . . . , X∗n) be independent random variables with Xi ~ ENH(αi, λ, β) (X∗i ~ ENH(αi∗, λ, β)), i = 1, . . . , n. Then, for any λ, β > 0, if (α1, . . . , αn) ≤ (α∗1, . . . , α∗n), that is, αi ≤ αi∗, i = 1, . . . , n, we have Xn:n ≥st X∗n:n.

quote: Theorem 3.4. Let X1, . . . , Xn (X∗1, . . . , X∗n) be independent random variables with Xi ~ ENH(α, λi, β) (X∗i ~ ENH(α, λ∗i, β)), i = 1, . . . , n. If 0 < α ≤ 1 and (λ1, . . . , λn) ≽w (λ∗1, . . . , λ∗n), then Xn:n ≥st X∗n:n.

quote: Theorem 3.5. Let X1, . . . , Xn (X∗1, . . . , X∗n) be independent random variables with Xi ~ ENH(α, λi, β) (X∗i ~ ENH(α, λ∗i, β)), i = 1, . . . , n. If 0 < α ≤ 1 and (λ1, . . . , λn) ≤ (λ∗1, . . . , λ∗n), that is, λi ≤ λ∗i, i = 1, . . . , n, then Xn:n ≥st X∗n:n.
family: ENH(α, λi, β) vs ENH(α, λi∗, β)

quote: Theorem 3.6. Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent random variables with Xi ~ ENH(α, λ, βi) and X∗1, . . . , X∗n be another set of independent random variables with X∗i ~ ENH(α, λ, βi∗), i = 1, . . . , n. Then, Xn:n ≥lr X∗n:n if and only if Σi=1^n βi ≥ Σi=1^n βi∗.

compared: sums of the β parameters (necessary and sufficient condition)
ambiguity: Necessary and sufficient condition (if and only if), since fn/gn ∝ (1 − e^{1−(1+λx)^α})^{Σβi − Σβi*}.

quote: Theorem 3.7. Let X1, . . . , Xn be independent random variables with Xi ~ ENH(α, λ, βi), and X∗1, . . . , X∗n be another set of independent random variables with Xi∗ ~ ENH(α, λ, βi∗), i = 1, . . . , n. Then for α < 1 and λ > 0, we have Σi=1^n βi∗ ≤ Σi=1^n βi < 1 ⟹ Xn:n ≥disp X∗n:n.
